approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs within each task. It breeds from high-score quantiles of a bounded, greedily retained population, uses connected-fragment crossover and local mutations with ordinary continuation, and admits fresh candidates under stable canonical identities. Its direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Before each allocation it fits a Gaussian process to every usable accepted observation, including offspring no longer in the breeding population. Folded Morgan counts and generalized Tanimoto covariance support correlated function draws over the complete fresh offspring pool. The current accepted-score mean and population standard deviation set both the training normalization and the raw units of predictions and draws; masked sampled maxima choose the announced batch.
approach.novelty: Remove only the repeated updating of that score normalizer: retain the mean, population standard deviation and floored scale from the first ordinary fit, while continuing to train on every newly accepted raw score. This tests the conditional contribution of adaptive normalization. The earlier initial-cohort control froze both training membership and normalization; this control keeps online data conditioning active. Other siblings changed target ranks, added residual-amplitude feedback or reserved a variance-seeking position. None isolated this existing normalizer while retaining the original full-archive correlated selector.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting uncertainty is the unisolated dependence of n-62daf219c70a on an evolving score normalizer inside an otherwise useful accepted-label predictor. Its actual three summary.json and run.log files mark all supplied replicas successful: macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747, and seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. A read-only audit of all fifteen actual task logs finds 435 full-archive fits, 60,900 generated training-row occurrences, 4,200 accepted next-fit probes, 4,350 generated accepted labels and no posterior fallback. Both normalization mean and scale differ from their first-fit values in all 420 later fits. The initial scale is 0.001 for the low-dispersion sitagliptin labels; contemporaneous Parent scales reach 213.613094 times that value, while docking reaches 59.397751 times its initial scale. In contrast, median_2 reaches a scale ratio as low as 0.704517. Applying fixed initial constants arithmetically to the already observed Parent archives would expose standardized magnitudes up to 720.661262; this is a passive exposure bound on Parent histories, not a Child outcome. The retained mean, raw uncertainty and effective raw noise therefore move together with accepted feedback, and the net value of that module is unresolved. n-7de8feaf821f jointly froze initial training membership and normalization, changed all 420 later same-pool selected sets and lost 0.15185627363148665 in paired macro score with all fifteen endpoints lower; it does not separate either operation. n-062b351ccb52 supplies real-label predictive influence for every nonterminal reserved final choice yet no later breeding of those identities and a paired loss of 0.022789878982636996. n-38bcd7569cce improves selected-stream interval coverage while losing 0.03814118675118202, with eight task-seed gains retained. n-ae12ccae8c7b changes every fitted target and selected set but lowers ordering correlation and loses 0.021067064526871015, with six endpoint gains including all median_2 cells. These specific counterexamples rule out treating normalization movement, predictive change, coverage or local wins as endpoint evidence; they do not establish that the present normalizer removal will help or harm.
hypothesis: Remove only ongoing recomputation of the GP score-normalization mean and scale by retaining the exact initial accepted-label normalization constants, while continuing full-archive raw-label conditioning and the inherited correlated posterior selector at every original fit.

finding_summary.headline: Adaptive normalization contributes: freezing it lowers mean final score by 0.03436
finding_summary.insights:
Updating the score mean and scale has positive conditional value even when the GP continues to learn from every new accepted label. The earlier control froze training membership and normalization together; this result narrows the answer to normalization without undoing that joint finding. It still does not separate centering from scaling, the associated change in raw observation noise, or their interaction with online training. The fixed scale becomes especially small relative to later score spread in docking and sitagliptin, whereas it exceeds the contemporaneous scale in median_2. These measured differences explain why raw uncertainty changes in different directions; they do not identify which consequence caused the endpoint loss.

More local parent wins, more reused breeders and slightly better same-stream prediction error are therefore insufficient evidence for useful search. The molecular assessment likewise finds fewer perceived scaffold families on every objective, but preserves useful aromatic amides, amines and alternative ring arrangements alongside reactive substituents, questionable ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry. That combination does not support a universal size, ring or heteroatom explanation, nor does it assign the score loss to one chemical motif. The passive reference has no rewards for omitted choices and no alternative future history, so mediation remains open. This complete exposed panel answers the registered normalization-only control under the current budget and composition; it supplies neither a broader claim that uncertainty should always increase nor a reason to retune this fixed control.
finding_summary.results:
The intended control executed while online learning remained active. All 435 fits retained every currently accepted raw label in order, with 4,200 generated labels entering their next fit and 150 final observations correctly censored. The first fit and selected batch matched the Parent in every task and seed. Fixed initial constants then differed from current-archive normalization in all 420 later fits. On the actual Child pools, the passive adaptive-normalization reference selected different sets in 401 of 435 batches; five additional batches differed only in order. Of 1,710 actually evaluated molecules absent from the reference sets, 1,641 entered a later fit and 1,016 later served as breeding parents. All evaluations completed.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.561314, a paired change of -0.034355 against the predicted loss scale of 0.002. Seed changes were -0.098249, +0.017166 and -0.021983; ten of fifteen task–seed endpoints declined and five improved. The Child had more generating-parent wins, 691 versus 629, but fewer sequential incumbent advances, 242 versus 258. Lower local prediction error also failed to translate into a better endpoint: on the same scored Child molecules, fixed-normalizer MSE was 0.005729 versus 0.005867 for the passive adaptive reference, while nominal 95% latent-interval coverage fell from 77.43% to 55.49%.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic series retain reactive substituents, uncertain ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This report describes n-c963c9fc454a against the published code Parent n-62daf219c70a. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile-mismatched seeds. All supplied Child and Parent trajectory paths, accepted-parent logs and seed summaries were present and read: 9000 paired trajectory records, including 870 optimizer proposals per task on each side. No task is omitted and no Parent comparison is absent. The record supports chemical description under the frozen batch size 10 and 300-observation budget, without an activation or contribution judgment. The Child produces compact aromatic amides and ketones, linked nitrogen heterocycles and arylamines, saturated cyclic diamines, medium-ring nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Its proposal median heavy-atom counts in the fixed task order are 24, 31, 33, 32 and 26; the corresponding medians for the Parent are 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. These are RDKit descriptions of trajectory structures, not new scores. Digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9943 to 0.9989 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.992 to 0.9989. These are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions or ring-diversity measurements. Charge and stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 on every task; neutral strings still contain available aliphatic amines. Recognizable medicinal chemistry coexists with N-halogen/O-F/S-Cl attachments, peroxide links, nitroso groups, aminal centres, small-ring unsaturation and difficult medium-ring connectivity. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable, with weak overall drug-likeness despite plausible individual frameworks. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with repeated families among many within-seed leaders. The Parent molecular report traces the recurring gaps to n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced them in its same-code profile baseline; that historical profile comparison is distinct from the complete current pairing. Current recurrence and counterexamples are stated below, without assigning the chemistry to a retained component. The read-only audit joins accepted parent records for every optimizer observation on both sides without an unresolved parent identity. This establishes ancestry reachability only. For example, the Child deco_hop seed-0 leader has recorded ancestors among initial evaluations 6, 7 and 8, while a generic initial-core substructure match points to initial evaluation 5, which is absent from that ancestry. Conversely, complete typed initial Murcko cores are absent from all Child seed leaders under the declared containment test despite their recorded founder ancestry. Neither result measures retained founder atoms, absence of shared fragments, nor scaffold-independent invention. Local atom-index snapshots in source are not used here as a persistent lineage atom map; actual atom provenance was not reconstructed. The full audit, citation receipt and source hashes are in .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r22-slot3-molecular/. Digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, not all seed incumbents. The supplied scores establish neither synthesis, stability, conformation nor biological activity.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader at evaluation 296 has 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings: a vinyl/methyl/methoxy indole region joined through a methylene-carbonyl linker to a pyridyl amide. Both the indole nitrogen and the amide nitrogen carry fluorine. Seed 1 instead reaches ordinary N-H indole carboxamides with a pyridyl ring and vinyl or vinyloxy substitution; seed 0 reaches a 23-heavy-atom benzimidazole/benzyl-ketone family with carbon-bound aryl halogens. Aromatic surfaces, carbonyl groups and ring nitrogen are abundant. The N-H amide and benzimidazole families have recognizable synthetic handles, but the leading double N-F example does not establish a routine stable target. The Parent leaders also have three aromatic rings and include N-halogen indole amides, a vicinal-diketone family and a cumulene-containing relative. All Child seed leaders have accepted ancestry reaching initial evaluation 9; that is not proof of conserved indole atoms.
liabilities: Fluorine on indole and amide nitrogen is chemically distinct from ordinary aromatic C-F substitution and raises local reactivity and handling questions.
N-O and N-S substitution also occurs among near-leaders; useful scaffold organization does not demonstrate the stability of these local environments.
Vinyloxy groups and terminal alkenes provide additional potentially reactive sites even in the otherwise recognizable N-H amide family.
missing_features: A consistently conventional nitrogen-substitution environment at the highest observed scores is missing: the overall leader uses two N-F bonds, although strong N-H and benzimidazole counterexamples already exist.

Chemically independent compact arrangements of the favorable aromatic and carbonyl regions are limited among leading within-seed variants; the evidence does not identify a missing target pharmacophore.
The molecule/score contrasts do not establish that more rings, more nitrogen, or more halogens would resolve the remaining objective gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. An N-H indole/pyridyl amide reaches 0.4330127018922193 in seed 1, and the seed-0 benzimidazole ketone reaches 0.4051924293365408. Replacing its aryl F with Br gives the same score at evaluation 294. The double N-F seed-2 leader reaches 0.47127110791377924; this does not isolate the effect of either N-F bond. A small aryl carbamate at seed 2/evaluation 47 scores 5.308608745558409e-08, and isolated F at evaluation 82 scores 0.0. Reward therefore associates with a combined compact aromatic/carbonyl organization in this record; halogen presence or a carbonyl alone is insufficient. The Parent seed leaders score 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081, respectively, in related but different molecular families. The Child improves some seed endpoints and lowers another without a uniform chemical-quality shift.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader at evaluation 289 has 29 heavy atoms and two benzene rings joined through an anilino-substituted carbon carrying a C-bound nitroso group, C-N=O. It also bears an aryl O-O-F chain, ethoxy, methoxymethyl, methylthio and carbon-bound fluorine. This is not an N-nitrosamine assignment. Seed 0 has a 30-heavy-atom linked aza-aromatic/dicarbonyl polycycle with five perceived rings and carbon-bound halogens. Seed 1 expands to a 48-heavy-atom assembly of five aromatic rings bearing alkynyl, ester, S-Cl and fluoroformate functionality. These are markedly different sizes and connectivities despite common aromatic richness. The Parent seed-0 leader is also 30 heavy atoms, but its linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione arrangement differs and includes O-F and chloromethyl-ether groups. Neither compactness nor the removal of one conspicuous local liability certifies feasibility.
liabilities: The O-O-F chain combines an O-O bond and an O-F bond; it is not ordinary carbon-bound fluorination. The O-O-O-C relative introduces another O-O bond.
The seed-2 C-bound nitroso functionality and its adjacent substituted amine deserve a separate reactivity assessment; graph validity and the observed score are not synthesis evidence.
The seed-1 leader includes an S-Cl bond and O-C(=O)-F functionality on a large polyaryl assembly; the seed-0 leader has dense ring junctions and unassigned centres despite lacking the O-O-F motif.
missing_features: Stable peripheral alternatives preserving the useful linked aromatic/heterocyclic relationships are not demonstrated at the leading scores; tied reactive substitutions leave that chemical question unresolved.

The favorable compact heterocyclic organization seen in the Parent seed-0 endpoint is not recovered by the Child leader in that seed; the trajectories do not reveal an exact missing motif or explain the causal reason.
Explicit stereochemical identity is missing at the nitroso-bearing saturated carbon and at potentially stereogenic centres in the dense seed-0 polycycle.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Methanol at seed 2/evaluation 11 scores 0.5, while the initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Child seed leaders reach 0.608874021711689, 0.6213400158269586 and 0.6287458379578247; their published Parent counterparts reach 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. Thus the formerly favorable seed-0 heterocyclic organization is not reproduced at its score despite equal leader size. Within Child seed 2, adding bromine to the methoxymethyl carbon leaves the leader score unchanged at evaluation 299. The related four-member fused sulfur-ring structure scores 0.6275118743149434; changing its O-O-F chain to O-O-O-C at evaluation 291 leaves that score unchanged. These ties show poor discrimination among chemically different peripheral liabilities, not a demonstrated need for any reactive bond. The higher scoring multi-region structures and low-scoring small fragments support context-sensitive organization, not a universal preference for larger molecules or more rings.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 1 reaches a 29-heavy-atom biphenyl/phenol structure bearing a bromomethyl group and an aminoalkyl linker to an N-propyl saturated six-member cyclic diamine. Its substituted aminal carbon is bonded to several nitrogen centres; this is not a simple piperazine assignment. Seed 2 reaches a 30-heavy-atom aryl-substituted five-member cyclic diamine joined through NH to an aminomethyl chroman-like ring system, with aryl thiols and carbon-bound halogens. Seed 0 instead retains a more elaborate 37-heavy-atom amine/thioamide/imine structure whose sulfur centre is drawn with both C=S and S=O bonds. Available aliphatic amines and aromatic surface are already prominent. The Parent includes simpler flexible tertiary-amine and pyrrolidine/fused-thioether families, so basic centres and ordinary saturated nitrogen rings are not missing capabilities.
liabilities: The seed-1 benzylic bromide is a distinct local reactivity concern from its ordinary aryl chlorine.
Nitrogen-rich aminal carbons and aryl thiols need environment-specific stability assessment; higher scores do not answer that question.
The seed-0 leader combines a nonstandard C=S/S=O centre, thioamide, imine and halogenated saturated carbons, with multiple unassigned stereochemical possibilities.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical identity of the successful cyclic aminals, aminoalkyl centres and chroman region is absent.

The Child leaders do not consistently combine the favorable aryl/basic-amine organization with simple robust linkages: bromomethyl, aminal, thiol and unusual sulfur environments remain. The Parent simpler amine families are counterexamples to an absolute inability to generate such chemistry.
Protonation and tautomeric states are not resolved by neutral SMILES; this does not imply that basic amines are absent or that a charged representation would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial N-sulfonyl cyclic-amine scaffold scores 0.01904115112334333, and an early N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine ketone scores 0.00021169315013374197. The Child seed-1 cyclic-diamine/biphenyl leader reaches 0.9946554741677153; the seed-2 cyclic-diamine/chroman leader reaches 0.99149345316924. The visibly different sulfur-rich seed-0 leader reaches 0.8060401103220081. This associates reward with presentation of available amines and aromatic regions, rather than nitrogen, sulfur or halogen count alone. Near the seed-2 leader, changing an aryl thiol to phenol gives the same 0.9887036102505549 score at evaluations 230 and 282, so thiol is not required in that local contrast. The Parent seed endpoints are 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012 for other aryl-amine organizations. These are oracle values, not measured affinity, selectivity or stability.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader at evaluation 256 has 35 heavy atoms, propyl/ethoxy groups, a fused aromatic [nH]-containing region and an adjoining N-methyl dicarbonyl/tertiary-amine ring. RDKit perceives ring sizes 6, 6, 9 and 9; the nitrogen-containing nine-member ring is aromatic-labelled. It should not be described as an ordinary indole solely from the [nH] notation. Seed 0 has a 30-heavy-atom bridged aryl/azaaryl ether-lactam structure with perceived rings extending to eleven members. Seed 2 has a 33-heavy-atom pyridyl/phenyl assembly joined to partially unsaturated N-N and dicarbonyl nitrogen rings. Familiar carbonyl, ether and amine groups coexist with challenging closures. The Parent also produces bridged nitrogen-carbonyl structures, including quinoline-linked medium rings; the Child changes these arrangements without demonstrating easier synthesis.
liabilities: Nine-member aromatic-labelled and nitrogen-dicarbonyl rings, and an eleven-member perceived ring in another leader, require geometry and synthesis assessment beyond sanitization.
The seed-2 N-N linkage and the crowded fused/bridged architectures are chemically specific concerns that are not captured by ring counts alone.
The seed-1 leader has no detected tetrahedral stereocentre in this parsing, a counterexample to treating every complex ring system as necessarily stereogenic; other leaders have unassigned centres.
missing_features: The leading aromatic/amine/carbonyl organization is not accompanied by a demonstrated simpler, geometrically credible connectivity at the same score.
Conformational and tautomeric identity of the aromatic-labelled medium ring, and stereochemical identity of the bridged and saturated seed-0/seed-2 systems, remain unspecified.
Ring-rich output and several distinct seed families already exist; the record does not support a generic need for additional rings or heteroatoms.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. Child seed leaders reach 0.21188996288820813, 0.24187632195949596 and 0.22036771749707829; the Parent leaders score 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. A small acid/anilide at seed 1/evaluation 14 scores 0.07504633196017493, and methyl chloride at evaluation 42 scores 0.008773280079294957. The ordering associates reward with combined aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl organization, but does not identify a missing target fragment. Replacing the seed-1 leader chlorine by methyl at evaluation 265 leaves 0.24187632195949596 unchanged; sulfur-containing or nitrile substituents reach 0.238116586384996. The exact local tie argues against a required halogen. The alternative expanded seed-1 arrangement can exceed its Parent endpoint even while the other seeds do not, countering a uniform claim that changing ring topology is always harmful.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 29 heavy atoms and a fused imino/carbonyl nitrogen heterocycle attached to a fluorophenol and a fluorinated cyclobutene bearing a difluoroamino group, N(F)F. Seed 1 reaches a 27-heavy-atom related fluorophenol/imino-carbonyl framework with a fluorinated cyclobutene and ordinary N-methyl substitution; it has no N-F bond. Seed 2 instead reaches a 25-heavy-atom fused imino/carbonyl heterocycle carrying N-F and a fluorophenol/fluoroethyl region without the small carbocycle. The Parent leaders include another small unsaturated heterocycle, a fluorinated alkenyl-dione family, and a five-member cyclic-cumulene/nine-member aza-ring system. The Child leaders do not reproduce that last extreme topology, but small-ring unsaturation and reactive nitrogen fluorination still occur.
liabilities: The seed-0 difluoroamino group contains two N-F bonds; the seed-2 N-F substitution is another environment requiring separate chemical assessment.
Cyclopropene and heavily substituted cyclobutene motifs introduce strain and stereochemical questions. Their presence is not proof that every small ring is infeasible.
A close substitution changes score sharply while leaving the rest of a questionable scaffold intact, so score sensitivity cannot certify the scaffold.
missing_features: A consistently conventional combination of fluorinated/polar regions with resolved nitrogen substitution and credible ring geometry is not established by the leading series. N-F-free and small-carbocycle-free leaders exist separately, so neither liability is unavoidable.
Explicit stereochemical identity of the substituted cyclobutene/cyclopropene centres is absent, and the imino/carbonyl heterocycles lack a resolved tautomeric description.
Alternative plausible frameworks preserving the observed local polar/fluorinated relationships are limited among the leaders; the data do not establish a missing target-specific pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. Child seed leaders reach 0.6038179407270375, 0.5992755709844388 and 0.5818612105822049; the Parent counterparts are 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. In a close seed-2 comparison, replacing the terminal aryl F of the leader by Cl at evaluation 296 gives 0.24039837831702202. The association is local fluorine placement in that whole framework, not a universal fluorination rule. The seed-0 cyclopropene relative at evaluation 293 scores 0.5758435922069238, while the N-F-free seed-1 cyclobutene reaches 0.5992755709844388. Thus neither N-F nor a particular strained ring is established as required. The truncated N-methyl fused imino heterocycle at seed 2/evaluation 69 scores 2.2905959046558152e-08, and ethyl methyl peroxide at seed 0/evaluation 12 scores 1.5655806596130004e-15; polarity without the larger organized framework is insufficient in these samples.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The source gap was documented in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by the same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a; the present evidence is n-c963c9fc454a against that published Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per objective. Current leaders include double N-F substitution, an O-O-F chain, C-bound nitroso chemistry, S-Cl, benzylic bromide and nitrogen-rich aminal centres. Tied peripheral variants can exchange one reactive group for another without changing the recorded score. Counterexamples are strong N-H amide and benzimidazole families, an N-F-free fluorinated heterocycle, and recognizable cyclic amines. The Parent also contains simpler aryl-amine frameworks. This is inconsistent environment control, not an inability to generate conventional functional groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while varying useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need chemically appropriate local alternatives that preserve favorable relationships learned from accepted feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens from heteroatom halogens and avoid treating a passing graph check as chemical feasibility. These observations do not establish that a universal rejection filter, bond replacement, or any particular component causes an endpoint gain; any intervention remains a separate hypothesis.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The source gap was documented in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by the same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a; the present evidence is n-c963c9fc454a against that published Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per objective. The current output includes substituted cyclopropenes/cyclobutenes, dense linked nitrogen polycycles and a leader with perceived ring sizes 6, 6, 9 and 9, including an aromatic-labelled nine-member nitrogen ring. Another leader has an eleven-member perceived ring. The historical Parent cyclic-cumulene extreme is not reproduced among the current leaders, so that exact manifestation is not claimed to persist unchanged. Ordinary saturated cyclic amines and compact N-H aromatic frameworks are counterexamples to a general inability to make credible rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control of ring geometry and unsaturation when constructing otherwise representable polycycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: De novo ring transformations need to distinguish feasible bond placement and junction geometry from merely valid connectivity, while retaining access to ordinary small, fused and saturated rings. Evaluate alternative topologies preserving learned functional relationships. Ring counts, aromatic labels and perceived smallest-ring sizes are descriptive; they neither certify a conformer nor establish the benefit of a ring constraint or component removal.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The source gap was documented in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by the same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a; the present evidence is n-c963c9fc454a against that published Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per objective. All current task digests have stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, and the full accepted structures have no specified tetrahedral centres in the audit. Cyclic aminals, substituted chroman regions, halogenated carbons and small unsaturated rings contain unassigned potential centres. Some aromatic leaders have no detected tetrahedral centre, so the issue does not apply to every molecule. Formal-charge incidence is separately 0.0 despite visible available aliphatic amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated molecular identities do not resolve stereochemistry at potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation and graph transformations should preserve or explicitly resolve chemically meaningful stereochemical identity when present, with appropriate treatment of achiral and configurationally unstable environments. Protonation and tautomerism require separate assessment. The record establishes unresolved identity, not a demonstrated stereochemical score penalty or evidence that every neutral molecule needs a charge.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The source gap was documented in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by the same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a; the present evidence is n-c963c9fc454a against that published Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per objective. Current output still includes isolated F, methyl halides, methanol and small peroxides near observed floors, while useful scores occur in combined aromatic/carbonyl or aryl/amine arrangements. A late methyl-halide proposal shows that context loss is not confined to initial exploration. Counterexamples include a compact two-aryl leader and high-scoring moderate-size cyclic amines; successful simplification exists. A much larger polyaryl leader in another seed and tied peripheral additions prevent a simple size-based interpretation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve enough functional-group context while avoiding both destructive fragmentation and unnecessary elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local accepted feedback to preserve useful relationships during fragment edits and to test simplifications or replacements of dispensable regions. This chemical gap does not justify fixed minimum size, automatic growth, or keeping every parental ring. Neither a fragment rejection rule nor a claimed causal role of a particular graph operator follows from the observed structural associations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The source gap was documented in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by the same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a; the present evidence is n-c963c9fc454a against that published Parent on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per objective. Many leading cohorts repeat aromatic-amide, cyclic-diamine or fused imino/carbonyl frameworks with local substitution changes; whole-panel ring richness and many unique strings do not establish useful independent scaffold coverage. The current accepted proposals have fewer generic Murcko scaffolds than the Parent on each supplied objective under the same descriptor, but endpoint directions differ by seed, and the medium-ring family shows substantial topological variation. Recorded ancestry can converge on an initial founder even without complete typed initial-core containment. A generic core match can also occur to an initial molecule absent from the accepted ancestry, directly countering an atom-retention interpretation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently produce chemically independent plausible alternatives to its leading within-seed families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic de novo scaffold transformations should offer feasible alternative connections among favorable functional regions and test them against real accepted feedback. Keep structural similarity, typed/generic scaffold containment, recorded breeding ancestry and actual atom provenance distinct. More unique scaffolds is not itself an endpoint benefit, a founder-use metric is not an atom-conservation metric, and the chemical association does not attribute convergence to normalization or any other retained component.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
